params.text:
A bilayer that builds itself

128 lipids are dropped into a box at random, water is poured in around
them, and then nothing else is done. Over the next 30 nanoseconds they
find each other, tails inward, heads out, and a membrane appears.

That is worth watching once, because it is the clearest demonstration in
the whole Martini set that the model is doing physics rather than being
told the answer. Nobody says 'make a bilayer'. The tails dislike water,
the heads like it, and a bilayer is what that adds up to.

It is also not guaranteed. Sometimes you get a micelle that never opens
out, or a bilayer with a water pore through it. Both are real
intermediates and worth seeing. If it happens, run it again -- the
starting arrangement is random. And the bilayer forms facing whichever
way chance picks -- usually not flat. 'Turn the membrane flat' checks,
and turns it, as the tutorial says to.

After that comes a second run with three settings changed, and those
three changes are the real lesson of the page. The note by the second
set of run settings says what they are and why each one matters.

1. THROW THEM IN AND SEE

One lipid, copied 128 times into a 7.5 nm box at random positions and
random angles, each copy rejected and retried if it lands on top of one
already there.

'How close is too close' is 0.21 nm here, not the 0.105 nm GROMACS uses
by default. That default is an atom's radius; a Martini bead stands for
about four heavy atoms and is roughly twice as wide. Leave it at the
default and the lipids are packed far too tightly to minimise.

The structure is the Martini 2 DPPC one, saved under the name DSPC. The
two have the same beads in the same places; what tells a C-16 tail from a
C-18 tail in Martini 3 is in the topology, not in the coordinates.

2. NOT VERY MUCH WATER

768 water beads, which is six per lipid. One Martini water bead stands
for four real ones, so that is 24 real waters a lipid -- thin. A real
membrane simulation would use several times more.

It is deliberate. With little water the lipids cannot get far from each
other, and a bilayer forms more reliably and sooner. It also means part
of the box starts out with no water in it at all, which is not realistic.

Worth trying: raise 'Most solvent molecules' and see whether you still
get a bilayer in 30 ns, or a micelle instead.

The same 0.21 nm bead size is used again, so water is not poured into
gaps a Martini bead could not actually fit into.

3. WHAT THE MOLECULES ARE

Four files, and the order they go in matters.

  martini_v3.0.0.itp                    what every bead type is
  martini_v3.0.0_ffbonded_v2.itp        how lipid bonds behave
  martini_v3.0.0_phospholipids_PC_v2.itp  the lipids themselves
  martini_v3.0.0_solvents_v1.itp        water

Bead types first, because everything below refers to them. General bond
behaviour before the specific lipids that use it.

The lipid files come from a separate place from the rest: the 2025 lipid
update lives in its own repository and is not in the Martini 3 release
archive. Both are downloaded here.

The counts -- 128 lipids, however many waters solvate managed to fit --
are read off the structure rather than typed. The tutorial asks you to
scroll back through the solvate output and find the number by eye.

params.raw:
; Minimisation, Martini 3.
; Walk downhill until nothing is pushing hard any more. No time passes.
integrator               = steep
nsteps                   = 10000

nstxout                  = 0
nstvout                  = 0
nstfout                  = 0

cutoff-scheme            = Verlet
nstlist                  = 20
nsttcouple               = 20
nstpcouple               = 20
rlist                    = 1.35
verlet-buffer-tolerance  = -1
pbc                      = xyz

coulombtype              = reaction-field
rcoulomb                 = 1.1
epsilon_r                = 15
epsilon_rf               = 0
vdw_type                 = cutoff
vdw-modifier             = Potential-shift-verlet
rvdw                     = 1.1

constraints              = none
constraint_algorithm     = Lincs
lincs_order              = 8
lincs_warnangle          = 90
lincs_iter               = 2

; Self-assembly, Martini 3. 30 ns at 20 fs a step.
;
; The pressure is the same in every direction (isotropic), which is right
; while there is no membrane yet -- the box has no special direction to
; treat differently. Once a bilayer has formed this becomes wrong, and the
; next run fixes it.
integrator               = md
dt                       = 0.02
nsteps                   = 1500000

comm-mode                = Linear
nstcomm                  = 100
comm-grps                = System

nstxout                  = 0
nstvout                  = 0
nstfout                  = 0
nstlog                   = 10000
nstenergy                = 1000
nstxout-compressed       = 1000
compressed-x-precision   = 100

cutoff-scheme            = Verlet
nstlist                  = 20
nsttcouple               = 20
nstpcouple               = 20
rlist                    = 1.35
verlet-buffer-tolerance  = -1
pbc                      = xyz

coulombtype              = reaction-field
rcoulomb                 = 1.1
epsilon_r                = 15
epsilon_rf               = 0
vdw_type                 = cutoff
vdw-modifier             = Potential-shift-verlet
rvdw                     = 1.1

constraints              = none
constraint_algorithm     = Lincs
lincs_order              = 8
lincs_warnangle          = 90
lincs_iter               = 2

tcoupl                   = v-rescale
tc-grps                  = System
tau_t                    = 1.0
ref_t                    = 340

gen_vel                  = yes
gen_temp                 = 340
gen_seed                 = 20130607

Pcoupl                   = c-rescale
Pcoupltype               = isotropic
tau_p                    = 4.0
ref_p                    = 1.0
compressibility          = 3e-4

params.text:
4. THE THREE SETTINGS THAT MATTER

The run above used one pressure for all three directions, which was right
while there was no membrane. Now there is one, and a membrane has a
direction: it is a sheet in the xy plane with water above and below --
turned that way, if it formed standing up, by the block just before.

SEMI-ISOTROPIC PRESSURE lets the area of the sheet and the height of the
box change independently. Keep them tied together and the membrane is
stretched or squeezed sideways by whatever the water column is doing, and
the area per lipid -- the number everyone quotes -- comes out wrong.

TWO THERMOSTATS, one for the lipids and one for the water. Heat crosses
the boundary between them slowly. With a single thermostat the water can
sit too warm and the membrane too cold while the average looks perfect.

TWO DRIFT GROUPS, for the same reason: the membrane can slide sideways
against the water, and correcting the box as a whole hides it.

Read the settings on the node -- all three are near the bottom, and the
comments in the file say the same as this note. Comparing it against the
self-assembly settings above is the exercise the tutorial sets.

This run is 10 ns, a third of the tutorial's 30, so that both runs fit
in a lesson. The area per lipid drops within the first nanosecond and
then keeps drifting slowly downwards: 10 ns does not settle it, which
is worth saying whenever the number is quoted.

params.raw:
; Equilibration of the bilayer, Martini 3. 10 ns at 20 fs a step: a
; third of the tutorial's 30 ns, so that both runs fit in a lesson. The area
; per lipid drops within the first nanosecond and then keeps drifting slowly
; downwards: 10 ns does not settle it, and the tutorial's 30 ns settles it
; further.
;
; Four things differ from the self-assembly settings, and they are the whole
; exercise on this page of the tutorial:
;
;   Pcoupltype = semi-isotropic. The box may now change its area and its
;     height independently. With one pressure for all three directions a
;     bilayer is squeezed or stretched sideways by whatever the height is
;     doing, and its area per lipid settles at the wrong value.
;
;   tc-grps = DSPC W, two thermostats instead of one. Heat crosses the
;     membrane-water boundary slowly, so with a single thermostat one side
;     can sit warm while the other sits cold and the average looks right.
;
;   comm-grps = DSPC W, likewise. The membrane can drift sideways against
;     the water; correcting the whole box as one hides that.
;
;   gen_vel = no, continuation = yes. The velocities come from the run
;     before -- through the structure file, which carries them -- rather
;     than being drawn fresh.
integrator               = md
dt                       = 0.02
nsteps                   = 500000

comm-mode                = Linear
nstcomm                  = 100
comm-grps                = DSPC W

nstxout                  = 0
nstvout                  = 0
nstfout                  = 0
nstlog                   = 10000
nstenergy                = 1000
nstxout-compressed       = 1000
compressed-x-precision   = 100

cutoff-scheme            = Verlet
nstlist                  = 20
nsttcouple               = 20
nstpcouple               = 20
rlist                    = 1.35
verlet-buffer-tolerance  = -1
pbc                      = xyz

coulombtype              = reaction-field
rcoulomb                 = 1.1
epsilon_r                = 15
epsilon_rf               = 0
vdw_type                 = cutoff
vdw-modifier             = Potential-shift-verlet
rvdw                     = 1.1

constraints              = none
constraint_algorithm     = Lincs
lincs_order              = 8
lincs_warnangle          = 90
lincs_iter               = 2

tcoupl                   = v-rescale
tc-grps                  = DSPC W
tau_t                    = 1.0 1.0
ref_t                    = 340 340

gen_vel                  = no
continuation             = yes

Pcoupl                   = c-rescale
Pcoupltype               = semi-isotropic
tau_p                    = 4.0
ref_p                    = 1.0 1.0
compressibility          = 3e-4 3e-4

params.text:
5. THREE THINGS TO MEASURE

DENSITY ALONG Z is the check that it worked. A bilayer gives water high
at both ends, a deep trough in the middle where the tails are, and the
whole thing symmetric about the centre. One flat line means no membrane.
Two humps and no trough means a micelle.

AREA PER LIPID is the number to compare against experiment: the area of
the box divided by half the lipids, since there are two leaflets. DSPC in
the fluid phase is about 0.65 nm2. Look at the curve as well as the
average -- the part at the start where it is still shrinking has not
equilibrated and should be left out.

HOW FAR A LIPID WANDERS, in the plane only. A lipid does not cross to the
other leaflet on this timescale, so counting the z direction would halve
the answer for no reason. The trajectory has to be unwrapped first, or a
lipid that leaves one side of the box and comes back on the other looks
as though it moved a whole box length in one step.

params.expected_label: DSPC in the fluid phase, from experiment
